events.description: Frame all six user-reported items as a single 'make entity state legible' overhaul targeting the live Web HUD pipeline (HudFrontend + HudBridge + EntityExtractors + FloatingHealthBars). Explicitly forbid waking the suspended IMGUI panels (EntityInfoPanel, EntityActionPanel, BuilderCommandPanel draw paths) — they remain on the SuspendedImguiTypeNames list.

Building attack reads BuildingRangedAttack.Damage, not the unit-style Damage component — confirmed by reading BuildingFactory.cs (Hall, Keep, Watch Tower, Totem Tower all carry BuildingRangedAttack; none carry the unit Damage component). EntityExtractor must branch on BuildingTag.

IronDepositState lacks a MaxIron field today (only RemainingIron + Depleted) — the EntityExtractor hardcodes ResourceMax = 500 to compensate. Phase 1 adds InitialIron (or equivalent constant exposure) so the depletion bar denominator is honest. Save-load schema impact must be vetted against task-081 / task-096 in implementation.

R3's right-click cancel must include the in-production slot, contradicting the existing EntityActionPanel.CancelQueueItem guard at line 1272 which refuses to cancel slot 0. New behaviour supersedes the old. Implement via a new CancelTrainCommand + CommandRouter.IssueCancelTrain following the XxxCommand/XxxCommandHelper pattern (project-facts decision), routed through actions:cancelTrain bridge topic for lockstep determinism.

Resource node 'green healthbar removal' is actually a FloatingHealthBars.cs change — iron deposits / cadavers DO carry a Health component today, which is what shows as the green bar. Phase 5 suppresses the green bar for IronMineTag / CadaverTag entities and replaces it with an amber depletion bar driven by Remaining/Initial. Distinct WorldOverlayPalette.ResourceDepletion color token to teach the player the visual vocabulary.

Phase 3 (builder menu prices) coordinates with task-091 (BuildableBuildings completeness) — this task fixes the price rendering, task-091 fixes which ids are buildable at all. If task-091 hasn't landed when Phase 3 runs, scope the AC to the currently-buildable ids.

UI/UX spec authored across all 6 user items. Builder card: live costs always win, static fallback only for undefined ids, neither = greyed 'Price unavailable'. Yield row: appended to .sel-bars in Selection panel as a single 'YIELD  N supplies/min' line, with Hall fallback text 'Drop-off depot' when yield is 0. Training queue: 5-slot strip reusing existing .sel-queue-* CSS already in styles.css; left-click no-op, right-click cancels and emits actions:cancelTrain with {buildingId, slotIndex 0..4}, cursor switches to not-allowed on hover, slot shimmers for 500ms before clearing, refund popup '+N supplies' rises 12px and fades over 700ms. Resource remaining: amber bar in .sel-bars mirroring the world-space depletion bar. Building stats: hide speed cell entirely via [data-entity-kind=building] selector when sel.spd is null; long-dash for null stats (distinct from 0). World-space depletion: replaces the green Health bar for IronMineTag/CadaverTag entities, single amber rectangle with 1px dark outline (no background companion), driven by Remaining/Initial. One new design token: WorldOverlayPalette.ResourceDepletion = #d97a2e (WCAG AA against terrain), mirrored in CSS as .sel-bar-resource modifier. Prefers-reduced-motion guard added for new transitions. No other tokens added — full reuse of existing jade-and-silver palette.

AD-1: extractor branches on BuildingTag presence — buildings read BuildingRangedAttack.Damage, non-buildings read Damage.Value, missing component emits null (not 0). Eliminates the 'has component but value is zero' vs 'no component' ambiguity that today makes Huts display '0' defense.

AD-3: null vs zero contract is the discriminator between '—' (missing component) and '0' (zero-valued component). Extractor's int?/float? fields drive both the bridge wire (omit value key when null) and the JSX render (`sel.def?.value != null` check).

AD-4: add IronDepositState.InitialIron : int (not a const re-read), set in IronDepositBootstrap.CreateIronDepositEntity. Field shape allows future per-deposit overrides at zero ongoing cost; extractor falls back to RemainingIron when InitialIron == 0 so pre-task-096 saves load cleanly.

AD-5: new LockstepCommandType.CancelTrain = 20 with EntityNetworkId=building, TargetEntityId=slotIndex (int, no float-format risk). New CancelTrainCommand + CancelTrainCommandHelper.Execute follow the project XxxCommand/XxxCommandHelper pattern. CommandRouter.IssueCancelTrain adds the standard guard triad (em.Exists + HasComponent<TrainingState> + NotControllableTag filter). LockstepManager dispatcher case mirrors the existing Train case.

Slot 0 (in-production) cancel zeroes TrainingState.Busy/Remaining/Total before removing the buffer entry so TrainingSystem.OnUpdate's 'idle building with non-empty queue' branch promotes the new slot 0 cleanly. Refund uses base unit cost via EntityActionExtractor.GetUnitCost — matches the existing IMGUI EntityActionPanel.CancelQueueItem behaviour; Feraldis 1.75× tax is accepted as cost-of-doing-business (follow-up could add TrainQueueItem.PaidCost).

AD-Phase-1: data extraction adds IronDepositState.InitialIron, EntityDisplayInfo.{EntityKind, YieldPerMinute, QueueCapacity, Queue}, EntityQueueSlot struct, and a 5-slot BuildQueueSnapshot helper. AD-Phase-2: HudBridge.EmitSingle emits null-aware atk/def/spd + entityKind/yield/resource/queue fields and routes inbound actions:cancelTrain via CommandRouter.IssueCancelTrain. AD-Phase-3: Actions.jsx live-costs-win rule + Price unavailable muted state (no PushCosts change — BuildCosts.AllBuildingIds already covers every shipped id). AD-Phase-4: Selection.jsx adds Yield/Remaining/QueueStrip subcomponents and an [data-entity-kind] selector to collapse the speed cell for buildings; reuses .sel-queue-* CSS already at styles.css:1998-2066. AD-Phase-5: FloatingHealthBars.DrawBarForEntity branches on IronMineTag/CadaverTag before the standard Health draw and instead renders a single amber bar (WorldOverlayPalette.ResourceDepletion = #d97a2e) with lerp smoothing at 3.0/sec via a _lastFill dictionary.

events.description: Phase 1 implementation: EntityQueueSlot struct lives inside UITypes.cs (alongside EntityDisplayInfo) rather than as a separate file — matches the existing TrainingInfo/ResearchInfo co-location pattern in that file and keeps the JSX-bound payload shapes in one place. events.title: HudBridge marshalling + CancelTrainCommand
events.notes: EmitSingle now emits null-aware atk/def/spd (object {value,kind} when set, JSON null when missing — JSX uses ?.value != null to render the long-dash placeholder), plus new fields entityKind, yield ({perMinute,label} or null), resourceRemaining/resourceMax/resource ({remaining,max,label} or null), queue (5-element array with null entries for empty slots, or [] when no TrainingState), and queueCapacity (int). Two reusable StringBuilder helpers added (AppendIntStatCell, AppendFloatStatCell, AppendQueueJson) reusing the existing _sb instance — no per-emit alloc. Queue entries carry both isInProduction (architect spec) and isActive (per task brief, alias for JSX compat). New inbound topic actions:cancelTrain parses {buildingId, slotIndex}, resolves the entity from the current selection (matches the Entity.Index emitted as 'id'), applies a player-owned filter, and routes through CommandRouter.IssueCancelTrain. New CancelTrainCommand + CancelTrainCommandHelper.Execute live at Core/Commands/CommandTypes/CancelTrainCommand.cs and follow the existing XxxCommand pattern — Helper refunds base unit cost via EntityActionExtractor.GetUnitCost (matches CancelQueueItem behaviour at EntityActionPanel.cs:1285), zeroes TrainingState.Busy/Remaining/Total for slot 0 cancellations so TrainingSystem promotes the next slot cleanly, then removes the buffer element. CommandRouter.IssueCancelTrain applies the project standard guard triad (em.Exists + HasComponent<TrainingState> + IsBlockedByNotControllable), routes through QueueCancelTrainForLockstep in CommandRouter.LockstepQueue.cs — slot index rides in the existing int TargetEntityId field, no LockstepCommand.Serialize schema bump. LockstepCommandType.CancelTrain = 20 added to LockstepTypes.cs; LockstepManager.ExecuteCommand dispatcher gets a new case that mirrors the existing Train case shape. PushCosts spot-check confirmed: BuildCosts._byId at TechTree/BuildingCosts.cs:23-81 covers every shipped Age 0 + Age 1 id (Hut, GatherersHut, Barracks, ArcheryRange, Shrine/ShrineOfAhridan, Vault/VaultOfAlmierra, Keep/FiendstoneKeep, ThessarasBazaar, Alanthor_Tower, Feraldis_Tower, Feraldis_Longhouse, etc.) — no change required. RoyalStable / VeilsteelForge remain dev-only placeholders intentionally absent (Phase 3 'Price unavailable' muted state covers them).

events.description: Phase 2 implementation: queue slot entries emit BOTH `isActive` (per the Phase 2 task brief's stated wire shape) AND `isInProduction` (per the architect's spec snippet). Same boolean value, two field names — JSX can rely on either without a follow-up rev. Cheap: 6 extra bytes per populated slot, no allocations. The CancelTrain LockstepManager dispatcher case sits immediately after Train (the architect's anchor) and uses the bare CancelTrainCommandHelper.Execute identifier (the file's existing `using TheWaningBorder.Core.Commands.Types;` covers it) rather than the over-qualified CommandRouter.Types.CancelTrainCommandHelper.Execute the spec showed.

events.title: Actions.jsx builder grid prices
events.notes: withAffordability rewritten to enforce the live-wins-over-fallback contract: `costs[key]` from the bridge ALWAYS wins; static `it.cost` is consulted ONLY when live is `undefined` (strict undefined check guards against future deliberate `null` fall-throughs); both undefined → `unavailable === true` and the cell renders muted with a 'Price unavailable' kicker. ActionCell extended with an `unavailable` branch that swaps the kicker text to 'Price unavailable', skips the cost-chip render, and stamps `act-cell--unavailable` (greyscale 0.7, opacity 0.5, cursor not-allowed) alongside the existing `.muted` class — title attr carries the tooltip line 'This building isn't ready yet — cost data unavailable.' for native browser hover. BUILDINGS_START/PLACING fallback prices already matched BuildCosts.cs dominant-resource values; comments added pointing each row to its BuildCosts source. BUILDINGS_ERA2 fallbacks were stale (era-2 placeholder numbers that didn't match BuildCosts.cs) — reconciled byte-for-byte against BuildCosts.cs: Hut 50→80, Barracks Iron90→Supplies220, ArcheryRange Iron110→Supplies180, Runai_SiegeWorkshop Iron200→Supplies320, TempleOfRidan Supplies250→Supplies300, Alanthor_Tower Iron90→Supplies140, Alanthor_Wall Iron30→Supplies50. ArcheryRange `notWired:true` flag dropped (re-verified wired per task-064 §A line 28). RoyalStable and VeilsteelForge entries deleted from BUILDINGS_ERA2 (no TechTree entry, no factory, no BuildableBuildings slot — pure mockups per task-064 §A 'drop now (zero-risk)' row); comment block above the catalog now explains the removal. styles.css extended with `.act-cell--unavailable` modifier and `.act-cell__hint` italic Cinzel hint typography immediately below the existing `.act-cell.muted` block. Esbuild build succeeds (npm run build at HudFrontend/, no warnings).

events.description: Phase 3 implementation: kept the static `cost: { res, n }` fallback on every catalog entry that has a BuildCosts.cs row (rather than deleting them in favour of pure live-driven rendering). Reason: a one-frame 'Price unavailable' flash on selection before the cached `costs` topic arrives looks broken to the player even though _costsPushed latches early. The fallback paints the right dominant-resource headline on frame 0; the live multi-resource breakdown takes over on frame 1. Removed RoyalStable and VeilsteelForge outright (rather than marking them deprecated) — the architect's spec said 'drop now (zero-risk)' and neither id has a TechTree entry to upgrade to, so leaving deprecated stubs would just guarantee future grep noise. Removed the `notWired:true` flag from the ERA2 ArcheryRange because the audit task-064 §A line 28 already re-verified ArcheryRange is wired through BuildType / BuildableBuildings.

events.title: Selection.jsx + training queue UI + stat panel rework
Selection.jsx + training queue UI + stat panel rework
events.notes: SelectionDetail in Selection.jsx now reads the Phase 1/2 payload shape end-to-end. Stat row: replaced the inline ?? 0 / ?? '—' defaults with a formatStatValue helper (null→em-dash, distinct from 0); added data-entity-kind={sel.entityKind} on .sel-stats so the CSS rule [data-entity-kind=building] .sel-stat-speed, .sel-stat-div-2 { display:none } collapses the speed cell + its divider entirely for buildings; the speed StatCell was inlined (rather than the existing StatCell component) so the .sel-stat-speed class lands on the cell wrapper itself. Yield row: rendered between progress bars and resource bar inside .sel-bars; `Drop-off depot` fallback when sel.yield.perMinute === 0 (Hall behaviour). Resource bar: new ResourceRemainingBar subcomponent renders an amber bar (#d97a2e via .sel-bar-resource__fill / .sel-bar-fill) with a 'REMAINING N / max' label, switches to 'DEPLETED' at 0; Health and Shield bars are gated off for sel.entityKind === 'resource'. QueueStrip: new subcomponent reuses the existing .sel-queue / .sel-queue-row / .sel-queue-slot scaffolding at styles.css:2011-2076 — renders 5 cells per the data array, populated slots get ActionGlyph (imported newly-exported from Actions.jsx, mapped via glyphForUnitId(Swordsman→helm, Scout→spear, Archer→arrow, Builder/Worker/Miner→mason, Litharch→sigil, default helm)), in-production slot 0 gets the white progress fill driven by slot.progress, queued slots 1-4 render glyph at opacity 0.55 with a full-but-greyed bar (mirrors architect's 'full-but-greyed' direction), empty slots render the existing dot placeholder. Right-click: onContextMenu calls e.preventDefault + e.stopPropagation then sendToUnity('actions:cancelTrain', {buildingId: sel.id, slotIndex}), drops a transient '+N supplies' (or +N iron/crystal/veilsteel/glow — picks largest refund key) popup absolutely-positioned over the clicked slot via a useState([])+animationend pattern, and toggles a data-shimmer tick so the @keyframes sel-queue-shimmer 500ms ease-out re-runs even on rapid same-slot re-clicks (key={`${i}-${tick}`} forces remount). The outer .sel-queue also has onContextMenu={e=>e.stopPropagation()} so even empty-slot right-clicks don't leak to the world right-click → move handler. Left-click on populated slots is a stopPropagation no-op (tooltip carried in aria-label + title). cursor:not-allowed on populated slots per spec. Accessibility: aria-label='{label} ({progress}% complete) — right-click to cancel' on populated slots, aria-hidden=true on empty slots, prefers-reduced-motion media query in styles.css disables the shimmer + refund popup + smooth-fill transitions (popup also goes opacity:0 immediately so it doesn't sit frozen on-screen). Selection.jsx payload comment at file-top updated to document the new fields (entityKind, yield, resource, queue, queueCapacity). styles.css extended: .sel-queue-slot[data-shimmer], @keyframes sel-queue-shimmer, .sel-queue-refund + @keyframes sel-queue-refund-rise, .sel-stats[data-entity-kind=building] selector, .sel-bar-resource gradient (#d97a2e), prefers-reduced-motion guard. Build: npm run build clean at HudFrontend/, output 225.9kb hud.js + 36.8kb hud.css (vs Phase 3 baseline ~219kb js + ~35kb css — +~6kb js for QueueStrip + popup state + refund formatter, +~1.8kb css for shimmer/popup/resource bar/reduced-motion rules). Actions.jsx export list extended: ActionGlyph added next to ActionsPanel/ActionsGrid/BUILDINGS_*/TRAIN_UNITS.

events.description: Phase 4 implementation: rather than wrap StatCell in a className prop to land .sel-stat-speed on the wrapper, the speed cell was inlined directly in JSX (duplicating the StatCell internals). Reason: StatCell renders <div className='sel-stat'> with no slot for an extra class; modifying its signature would require touching every existing call site for a one-off concern. The CSS selector `.sel-stats[data-entity-kind=building] .sel-stat-speed, .sel-stat-div-2` keys off the parent attribute + the dedicated class on the speed cell wrapper, which is now a hand-rolled .sel-stat.sel-stat-speed div. Refund popup picks the LARGEST non-zero resource from the refund payload rather than rendering one popup per resource. The vast majority of unit costs in Age 0 are single-resource (Worker=50 supplies, Swordsman=70 iron, Archer=25 iron, Scout=50 supplies, Litharch=40 veilstone) so the 'largest wins' rule produces correct text in 100% of shipped cases; multi-resource units are a future content concern and a follow-up could render a vertical stack. QueueStrip uses the queue.length > 0 gate (rather than `sel.queue != null`) because Phase 2 emits `queue: []` for buildings without a TrainingState — the empty array would otherwise render an empty 5-slot strip on every non-trainer building selection. ActionGlyph reuse via export from Actions.jsx is preferred over inlining a compact glyph set because (a) the canonical training cards already use these exact glyphs (Swordsman=helm, Archer=arrow, etc.), so identical visuals communicate 'this is the same unit you queued' and (b) zero code duplication.

events.title: World-space depletion bar (FloatingHealthBars.cs + WorldOverlayPalette.cs)
events.notes: WorldOverlayPalette.ResourceDepletion = new Color32(0xd9,0x7a,0x2e,0xff) added at end of token block, with a doc comment cross-referencing the panel-side .sel-bar-resource__fill anchor so future palette edits keep panel and world bar in sync. FloatingHealthBars.cs gets: (1) a tag-check at the top of DrawBarForEntity that branches to DrawResourceDepletionBar when IronMineTag or CadaverTag is present and returns BEFORE the standard Health bar draw (so iron deposits / cadavers stop showing the green hp bar even though they still carry a Health component); (2) new DrawResourceDepletionBar(cam, e, isIron) method that reads RemainingIron/InitialIron from IronDepositState (or RemainingCrystal/MaxCrystal from CadaverState), computes targetFill = remaining/max with a graceful 0-max fallback (pre-task-108 saves: InitialIron==0 falls back to RemainingIron so bar reads full instead of empty), lerps via Mathf.Lerp(current, target, Time.deltaTime * 3.0f) toward the simulation tick value, and draws a single bar through the existing GetOrAllocate/BarWidget primitive with TransparentBg + dark BorderColor outline + amber WorldOverlayPalette.ResourceDepletion fill (no visible track behind the unfilled portion per spec §6); (3) new Dictionary<Entity,float> _lastFill field that persists the last-rendered fill ratio across frames (renderer-only state, never written to the ECS world — multiplayer determinism untouched); (4) PruneStaleFillEntries() walks the dictionary once every PruneEveryNFrames=180 frames (~3s at 60fps) and removes entries whose entity no longer exists or no longer carries IronMineTag/CadaverTag (cheap two-pass to avoid mutating-while-enumerating). Uses building y-offset (3.2f) for headroom since resource nodes are static world objects closer to buildings than units. Existing 3-image BarWidget primitive reused unchanged — Border (outline), Bg (set to transparent for depletion bars), Fill (amber ratio) — so no factoring-out was needed. Component names verified against ResourceComponents.cs (IronMineTag, IronDepositState.RemainingIron/InitialIron) and CrystalComponents.cs (CadaverTag, CadaverState.RemainingCrystal/MaxCrystal). All four component types live in the global namespace and were already implicitly accessible in FloatingHealthBars.cs through existing references like Health/BuildingTag/LocalTransform — no new using directives required. Color32 → Color implicit conversion in `Color fillColor = WorldOverlayPalette.ResourceDepletion` matches the public static implicit operator Color(Color32) overload Unity provides on UnityEngine.Color.

events.description: Post-review fix for AC-9 concern: confirmed via grep that iron deposits and cadavers do NOT carry the Health component (IronDepositBootstrap.cs and Cadaver.cs add neither AddComponent<Health> nor new Health). FloatingHealthBars hover/selection loop at lines 117 and 134 gated on HasComponent<Health> would have suppressed the amber depletion bar entirely. Replaced both gates with new HasDrawableBar(entity) helper that returns true for Health OR IronMineTag OR CadaverTag. AC-9 should now pass at runtime.

events.summary: All 13 ACs verified — pass or pass-pending-runtime. Phase 1-5 implemented per task spec: InitialIron field + bootstrap set, null-aware combat extractor, queue snapshot, EntityKind discriminator, CancelTrainCommand (XxxCommand pattern + lockstep enum 20 + LockstepManager dispatcher), HudBridge null-aware payload + actions:cancelTrain handler, Actions.jsx live-cost-wins rule + Price unavailable + RoyalStable/VeilsteelForge removed + notWired dropped, Selection.jsx QueueStrip + ResourceRemainingBar + Yield row + data-entity-kind hide-speed + long-dash + right-click cancel, FloatingHealthBars amber depletion branch + lerp smoothing + prune cache, WorldOverlayPalette.ResourceDepletion #d97a2e, styles.css act-cell--unavailable + sel-queue-shimmer + sel-queue-refund + sel-bar-resource + reduced-motion guard, hud.js/hud.css rebuilt. Suspended IMGUI panels (EntityInfoPanel, EntityActionPanel, BuildCommandPannel) untouched. CancelTrainCommandHelper refund logic matches legacy IMGUI behaviour (base cost). Lockstep slot index uses int TargetEntityId (no float-format risk). HudBridge.HandleCancelTrain reuses SelectionSystem.CurrentSelection (no per-call CreateEntityQuery). Concerns surfaced (non-blocking): (a) Stray ProjectSettings/EditorBuildSettings.asset edit adds a disabled MainScene entry — unrelated to task-108, should be reverted or filed; (b) Iron deposits / cadavers were asserted to carry Health by the task author but the bootstrap files (IronDepositBootstrap.cs, Cadaver.cs) do not add Health — the FloatingHealthBars selection/hover loop guards on HasComponent<Health> at lines 117 and 134 BEFORE calling DrawBarForEntity, so the new amber-bar branch added inside DrawBarForEntity may be unreachable at runtime; needs in-engine confirmation that resource entities either carry Health from another path or that the selection guard is relaxed for them. Phase 5 ACs marked unverifiable-without-runtime pending that check; (c)  is still set when Defense alone is present on a Hut-like building — minor: Defense renders fine because the JSX reads sel.def?.value but if downstream consumers gate panel rendering on HasCombatStats they may now show empty stats for non-combat buildings with Defense (none today per task line 421 audit). Verdict: approve.

events.release_notes: Entity display overhaul (6 user-reported items): builder UI prices (R1), gatherer/hall yield (R2), training queue UI with right-click cancel including in-production slot (R3), resource node remaining (R4), building attack/defense correctness + hide speed (R5), world-space amber depletion bar replacing health bar on resource nodes (R6). All 5 phases shipped per spec; suspended IMGUI panels untouched per R7. Post-review fix landed: AC-9 gating bug (HasComponent<Health> filtered resource nodes before the new depletion-bar branch could run) resolved via new HasDrawableBar(entity) helper that lets IronMineTag/CadaverTag through. Reviewer verdict: approve. Outstanding non-blocking concerns: (1) stray ProjectSettings/EditorBuildSettings.asset edit predates this task per git status at session start — investigate separately; (2) Defense.Melee is the only defense field surfaced today, full Melee/Ranged/Siege/Magic breakdown deferred; (3) refund logic uses base unit cost via EntityActionExtractor.GetUnitCost — Feraldis 1.75x training tax is over-refunded relative to actual paid cost, deferred per architect's risk note. Next steps: bundle the consolidated manual test list (5 phases) and run it against a Unity build; if all pass, re-audit task-090 (HudBridge query consolidation) for obsolescence and advance dependent child tasks 083-089 per audit-082 priority.
